extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) tailored to evaluating logical reasoning, algebraic reasoning, and scientific reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing multimodal datasets, puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic paper figures from Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates, specifically selecting examples with numeric answers or quantity words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, and discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process resulted in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%, with only 6 disagreements among 736 newly collected questions, which were resolved through discussion.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process, with commitments to maintain the datasets, refine potential data noise based on community feedback, and evolve the leaderboard.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include potential gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals, and a lack of unified format and structure in annotations due to the heterogeneity of sources.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for mathematical reasoning intertwined with visual understanding.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: MATHVISTA incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering (MathQA) datasets and 19 VQA datasets. In addition, we have created three new datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA)

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: MATHVISTA incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets... In addition, we have created three new datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) which are tailored to evaluating logical reasoning on puzzle test figures, algebraic reasoning over functional plots, and scientific reasoning with academic paper figures, respectively.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: IQTest comprises 228 examples requiring inductive reasoning, abstract thinking, pattem prediction, and calculations, sourced from puzzle test figures on online leaming platforms... PaperQA is a novel dataset featuring questions derived from informative academic illustrations, including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we initially designed heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words (as listed in §D.1) in the questions were selected.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To ensure data quality, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. To ensure consistency in annotation, we employed a two-step process. Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers... Then, these discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring a consensus was reached on each example.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Specifically, among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers. Then, these discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring a consensus was reached on each example.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: One limitation is the dataset coverage. While MATHVISTA encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals... Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples (Table 1) having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Our dataset, MATHVISTA , is therefore motivated to bridge this gap, offering a robust evaluation benchmark for mathematical reasoning intertwined with visual understanding, thus pushing AI assistants towards general-purpose capabilities.
